sources.supports: Candidate-city eligibility only: Shanghai, Nanjing, Suzhou, Nantong, Ningbo-Zhoushan, Wuhu, Anqing, Jiujiang, Wuhan and Chongqing are listed as port-type national logistics hub carriers.

sources.publisher: Central Committee of the Communist Party of China and State Council
sources.supports: Functional roles: Shanghai core, Taicang feeder and near-sea container role, Ningbo-Zhoushan development, Nanjing-below river-sea transport, Wuhu-Maanshan hub and port-rail access.
Candidate-pool evidence for major inland ports and the Yangtze Delta high-grade waterway network; not evidence of a service between every listed port.
Guoyuan Port is an operational water-rail-road multimodal hub; Yuzui freight station and container facilities are described.
Facility-level evidence for the Yangluo port-area container rail-water demonstration project and railway loading yard.
Guoyuan-Waigaoqiao water commitment within 192 hours and Guoyuan-Yangshan routing via Waigaoqiao or Taicang within 240 hours.
The Shanghai-Chongqing express water corridor links Chongqing Port, Taicang Shanggang Zhenghe terminal and Shanghai Port including Waigaoqiao and Yangshan.
Ordinary Chongqing-Shanghai water time of 11-12 days, express time of 8-9 days and over 3000 sailings/718000 TEU by June 2022; the express service does not call at intermediate ports.
Luchaogang railway centre is operational and linked to Yangshan by a separately managed last-mile road drayage operation; proposed facilities are distinguished from existing operations.

Shanghai reported Chongqing among 27 cities connected to Shanghai Port sea-rail services and stated that the Shanghai endpoint for those city services was Luchaogang centre station. Chongqing was not among the six named fixed-cycle daily lines, so this does not establish a daily Chongqing service or its current origin station.

Shanghai reported more than one million TEU of sea-rail traffic in 2025, 1.2 million TEU annual Luchaogang handling capacity, three minutes per container handling operation and a 40 percent increase in total daily sea-rail trains. These are network-level operating facts, not a Chongqing timetable or total dwell time.

The 2024 project self-assessment reports that more than 60 percent of measured rail-to-port transfer operations at Luchaogang-related projects were completed within one hour. It does not publish a full dwell-time or gate-queue distribution.

The Yangpu-Tuanjiecun Chongqing-Shanghai five-fixed container train was trialled at one train per week, 40-48 containers per train and 55-60 hours in transit. It is historical corridor evidence, not proof of a current Guoyuan-Luchaogang train.

The operator reports two Chongqing-Shanghai sailings per week, ten days running time, 700-800 TEU and 9600-11000 tonnes per week, with ten 345-434 TEU vessels. The precise Chongqing and Shanghai terminals are not identified.

sources.publisher: Chongqing Municipal Government Port and Logistics Office
sources.supports: The published water-export process leaves booking lead time to the shipper or agent, gives one hour for arrival reporting and unloading, one hour for a single-container loading operation and a 20-hour total for non-inspected export-port processing. This is a process commitment, not a booking-wait distribution.

sources.publisher: Chongqing Municipal Government Port and Logistics Office
sources.supports: The authority states that operational measures improved Chongqing-Shanghai water punctuality by 50 percent. No baseline or absolute on-time percentage is published, so an absolute reliability distribution cannot be reconstructed.

In the first half of 2025 the express corridor recorded 647 sailings and 204000 TEU, with an example 388-TEU vessel sailing from Guoyuan toward Taicang in eight days. These are aggregate corridor operations, not operator-specific booking reliability or completed order records.

One public marketplace posting offered a loaded single 20-foot container from Yitian Road in the Luchaogang area to Yangshan for CNY 200 at 17-21 tonnes. This is a spot observation, not a contracted sea-rail tariff or completed-trip record; personal contact details are not retained.
Industry-association evidence states that Luchaogang centre is about 45 km by truck from Yangshan and identifies drayage as an additional chain cost.
For eligible 2025-2026 Luchaogang sea-rail operations, signed last-mile road operators receive CNY 180 per loaded TEU and CNY 130 per empty TEU. This is operator support, not the customer's tariff.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Transport, National Railway Administration and China State Railway Group
sources.supports: The official casebook identifies Shanghai Port sea-rail operators, daily Luchaogang-Chengxiang service, port-road-rail handoff, one-container operation and the then-applicable CNY 180 last-mile support. It is a Chengdu case and is not used as Chongqing linehaul time.
Wuhu-Shanghai Yidong domestic direct route and Wuhu-Waigaoqiao foreign-trade direct route were added in 2020.
The Wuhu-Shanghai five-fixed liner had a port-stay commitment below eight hours and voyage commitment below 60 hours; published scope does not resolve the Wuhu port area.
Zhujiangqiao is the container/foreign-trade hub and Yangshan feeder; Yuxikou is a coal rail-water hub. It also reports the Wuhu-Shanghai core route and provincial feeder structure.
Facility-level rail access and cargo roles for Zhujiangqiao, Sanshan and Yuxikou port areas; planned works remain planning evidence.
Nanjing Longtan port-area railway special line passed completion acceptance and supports road-rail-water intermodal handling.

sources.publisher: Jiangsu State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission
sources.supports: Nanjing-Shanghai sea-rail daily service was reported as operational; Changzhou Donggang-Yangshan river-sea service was also reported.
Longtan port-Longtan station-Yangshan daily service and Jiangdu-Longtan rail-water chain; route descriptions do not publish a complete tariff/time/distance tuple.

sources.publisher: Jiangsu State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission
sources.supports: Qiba-Longtan-Waigaoqiao foreign-trade feeder route with a reported 25-hour voyage.
Longtan and Taicang are core river-sea-river hubs; Nanjing, Suzhou and Nantong are intermodal hubs. Some named facilities are future projects.
Taicang's port-hub and container role; the port railway was described as a project and is not backdated as operational.

sources.publisher: Zhejiang Provincial Department of Ecology and Environment
sources.supports: Chuanshan railway branch and station, completed in 2019, support port rail-container operations.
First Sichuan-Nantong Tonghai-Zhejiang rail-water container movement; current-reference evidence only.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Transport / Yangtze River Shipping Development Research Center
sources.supports: September 2024 average 20-foot export feeder rates: Chongqing-Shanghai FIO CNY 1112, Wuhu-Shanghai Yangshan FIO CNY 418 and Nanjing-Shanghai FIO CNY 294. FIO is not a door-to-door quote.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Transport / Yangtze River Shipping Development Research Center
sources.supports: August 2025 Chongqing-Shanghai averages: CNY 1130 per 20-foot FIO export-feeder box and CNY 1547 per 20-foot CY domestic box. The model uses FIO only for the export-gateway case and does not treat it as door-to-door.
Indicative Chongqing-Shanghai 20-foot comparison: road CNY 15000, rail CNY 4600 and water CNY 1400; exact inclusions are not stated.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Transport and partner agencies
sources.supports: Chengdu-Shanghai case with road, rail, rail-water and all-water times and costs; used only as a cross-corridor time proxy where explicitly labelled.
Default freight emission factors used by the model: road 0.076, rail 0.003 and water 0.020 kgCO2e per tonne-kilometre.

China road-freight default values aligned with ISO 14083 and GLEC provide diesel tractor TTW and WTW intensities by gross vehicle weight under a 93 percent load factor and 19.5 percent empty-running assumption. They are equipment-sensitive defaults, not measurements of this corridor's trucks.

sources.publisher: State Administration for Market Regulation and Standardization Administration of China
sources.supports: GB/T 32151.30-2024 is the current greenhouse-gas accounting and reporting standard for water-transport enterprises, effective 2025-04-01. It defines an accounting route but does not disclose Haohang vessel fuel or load data.

A public 2025-2026 container-drayage procurement specifies 20GP or 40GP rail/water containers, 19-27 tonnes per loaded container and named factory/warehouse-to-Guoyuan-or-Tuanjiecun origin legs. It is a procurement profile, not a Chongqing-Shanghai completed-order dataset.
Luchaogang is about 30 km from the main Yangshan port area and the East Sea Bridge is 32.5 km; this is a geographic lower-bound reference, not a complete drayage distance or tariff.

Team-collected city-pair model inputs. Relevant rows: Chongqing-Shanghai road 1695 km, rail 1733 km, water 2399 km; Wuhu-Shanghai water 488 km; Nanjing-Shanghai water 392 km. These are not government observations or facility-to-facility measurements.
Historical generic road-rail transfer parameters: 50 h/1000 t, 2 CNY/t and 0.128 kgCO2e/t. Mapping them to Luchaogang is a model assumption, not an observed terminal tariff.
